security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel code compiled with CSR address constants matching the old (pre-fix) spec reads or writes CSRs 0x348 (old MSP, now MIPREEMPTCFG), 0x148 (old SSP, now shifted to 0x149), 0xFB1 (old MITHRESHOLD, now 0x347), or 0x1B1 (old SITHRESHOLD, now 0x147). On hardware implementing the corrected spec, each access targets a different architectural CSR than intended — most critically, writing the M-mode stack pointer to 0x348 instead writes the interrupt preemption configuration (MIPREEMPTCFG), and reading from 0xFB1 hits a custom-machine CSR address that hardware may treat as unimplemented (trap) or aliased (silent garbage).
security_spec.summary: CSR address reallocation collides old msp (0x348) with new mipreemptcfg (0x348), so kernel code using stale #define constants writes stack pointer context into interrupt preemption config — silently disabling or re-enabling interrupt preemption — and old mithreshold (0xFB1) moves from custom space to 0x347, making any kernel access to 0xFB1 either trap (DoS) or hit an unrelated vendor CSR.
